A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CSF/METRA study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and can be matched reliably, including renumbered and relocated material.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendices B–C report original reinforcement-learning experiments, including exploration, goal reaching, hierarchical control, representation analyses, and ablations.

after.justification: The original empirical results are retained, with additional METRA sensitivity experiments and a qualitative report of unsuccessful MiniHack experiments.

M1.justification: CSF's contrastive representation objective, intrinsic reward, successor-feature critic, and policy updates remain unchanged in Section 5 and Algorithm 1. The MiniHack report does not document a new method component or procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: The six existing benchmark environments are retained. New Appendix C.6 reports testing CSF and METRA on MiniHack-Corridor-R5-v0, extending coverage to discrete-action, partially observed navigation between five rooms, although results are only qualitative.

E2.justification: METRA, CIC, DIAYN, DADS, and VISR retain their participation in the corresponding existing comparisons. The added MiniHack experiment uses the existing comparator METRA; no new baseline method is introduced.

E3.justification: Appendix C.4 adds separate Ant sweeps over METRA's initial dual variable, slack variable, and dual learning rate. Existing benchmark metrics, model configurations, and goal-reaching and hierarchical-control procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.4 and Figure 11 examine METRA's sensitivity to three dual-optimization hyperparameters. Appendix C.6 adds a brief failure case study on MiniHack. Existing representation analyses, design ablations, and skill-dimension and CSF scaling-coefficient studies are retained.

E5.justification: The added METRA sensitivity study explicitly reports means and standard deviations over two seeds. The existing ten-seed main comparisons and five-seed CSF scaling study retain their reporting; no change to their run counts is stated.

E6.justification: Figure 11 adds learning curves showing broadly similar Ant coverage across the tested METRA hyperparameters. Appendix C.6 newly reports that neither CSF nor METRA achieved consistently stable MiniHack performance. Existing benchmark curves, numerical findings, and rankings are retained.

T1.justification: The propositions, assumptions, corollary, and appendix derivations remain substantively unchanged. Appendix A.4 changes the notation for the same variational distribution from qπ to q̃ without changing the argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims that METRA can be interpreted within MISL and that the simpler CSF method achieves comparable performance. The shortened conclusion does not materially change their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C.6 newly conjectures that discrete actions, randomized initial states and room layouts, and partial observability explain the MiniHack difficulties. This adds a concrete applicability concern, while the earlier broader scaling limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Figure 11 newly specifies tested hyperparameter values spanning initial λ of 0.1–100, slack of 10^-6–10^-1, and dual learning rates of 10^-6–5×10^-3. Existing implementation, hardware, and code disclosures are unchanged; the new reproducibility statement mainly consolidates pointers to them.

R1.justification: v2 adds Samvelyan et al. (2021) for MiniHack. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to MISL, contrastive learning, successor features, and METRA otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized edits and condensation in Sections 6–7, adds a reproducibility statement and conference headers, and inserts two appendix subsections. The broader narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the three-panel Figure 11 and adjusts the surrounding appendix layout. The existing trajectory visualization becomes Figure 12 and is repositioned, while other changes concern figure sizing, captions, spacing, and headers.

improvement.justification: The added METRA sensitivity checks provide useful evidence about the hyperparameters removed by CSF, and the MiniHack failure report makes applicability limits more transparent. These are modest gains: the sensitivity study uses only two seeds, and MiniHack lacks quantitative results and detailed settings. The core method, theory, and established benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
